> config: https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#precedence-order

The precedence order documentation does not reflect that the built-in's are part of the opencode codebase. There is in effect a missing layer of config from this precedence order.
 
> Built in agents arent on a file on ur machine, they are part of opencode itself so u can override, delete, manage them in ur config but they wont appear on ur file system

Personally I very much do not like this design decision as it creates 'config' that is not visible to the user and it is not documented where that config is located. It also results in confusion about what config exists and therefore what the user might want to overwrite.

> Previously opencode wouldn’t automatically create a config file, we changed this since it confused people.

Automatically creating an empty config file is similarly confusing - users are left looking for the 'real' config file that is producing the default behaviour. The approach that I'm used to and personally prefer, is to create the config file with the default configuration rather than having undocumented config as a part of the application. That way you can see what config produces the default behaviour which is a useful example and there is not mysterious seemingly missing config.

It is also commonplace to distribute config files with example config in place and commented out.

> Things in ~/.local/state/opencode/... are not meant to be manually edited, u dont need to place configs there that is where the app tracks some state stuff for tui and otherwise.

This location should still be recorded in the docs as it is useful to know where this information is being stored if you want to see the prompt history file for example. It should just be indicated that these are not intended to be user editable.

> OpenCode has a customize-opencode skill now to help w/ cases like this, but asking this question against openai models ig they have the answer in their training data so its not even necessary

Just because these models can currently answer this question does not mean that this should not be documented properly, or indeed at all models will correctly answer this question.

My use-case is setting up and entirely local setup without querying any cloud based models so the customise opencode skill of of no use to me until I have configured access to a local model to use that skill - you see the catch 22.

Thanks for flagging these. #29216 is distinct from each:

**vs #24948 and #22828 (auto vision fallback / auto transcription)**

Both propose a server-side automation — automatically call a separate vision model to transcribe the image into text, then feed that text to the non-vision model. This is a heavyweight feature with config, model selection, and a processing pipeline.

#29216 is much simpler and more fundamental: **just don't strip the image.** The non-vision model doesn't need to read the image itself — it only needs the image reference (file path / MIME / filename) so it can decide to dispatch the image to a vision-capable MCP tool. This is the tool-delegation pattern — the model says "I can't see this, let me call `analyze_image` on it." An auto-fallback does the work silently; the tool-delegation pattern gives the model agency.

**vs #23508 (provide full image path in error)**

The closest in spirit, but #23508 asks for a better error message. #29216 argues there shouldn't be an error at all. The image should pass through as **context the model can reason about**, not as an error it must apologize for. The difference: #23508 says "tell me where the image is" → #29216 says "don't destroy the image reference in the first place."

**vs #26668 (clipboard auto-read)**

Unrelated bug — that's about clipboard images being auto-attached even for text-only messages. #29216 is about intentionally uploaded images being stripped.

---

**Summary**: All four existing issues assume the model must either natively support images or get a text transcription. They all work within the assumption that the `unsupportedParts()` rejection is correct behavior. #29216 challenges that assumption: the model doesn't need to support images — it just needs an un-destroyed reference so it can route to tools.

The fix is also simpler than #24948/#22828: change `unsupportedParts()` to emit a text part with file metadata instead of a hard error — no model routing, no config, no transcription pipeline needed.
